summary: Beth Glenfield from DevDay argues that AI has fundamentally broken technical hiring. She opens by asking whether the audience uses AI in recruitment, competes with Google/Meta for talent, and recognizes LeetCode puzzles no longer indicate who can build great AI products. She frames 2025 as a year where the technical recruitment process is broken and small companies are being crushed in the talent war. She cites Clu, an AI cheating service from an ex-Columbia student that raised $5.3M and is approaching $1M ARR, achieving 93% LeetCode Wizard success rates at Google and Meta interviews. One in three interviews now involve AI assistants, meaning interviewers are effectively testing who has the best AI coding assistant. She references Sam Altman's advice to learn the best AI tools and Marc Benioff's claim that Salesforce achieved 30% productivity boosts replacing engineers with AI. She notes candidates now choose between startups and Google's AI division based on brand, prestige, and perceived stability, not just compensation. The candidates companies actually want—creative problem solvers, collaborative leaders, those who work with AI—are building AI tools, contributing to open source, and understanding business impact, none of which LeetCode measures. DevDay's alternative replaces coding interviews with real-life workplace simulations where candidates collaborate with AI agents having distinct personalities (perfectionist, pragmatist, security expert, junior developer needing mentoring). This measures collaboration with AI, ambiguity handling, communication in PRs and tickets, mentoring, and adaptability. She notes big companies can brute-force hiring but most companies cannot afford a bad hire costing 20-60K. She references Zuckerberg's prediction that AI will handle mid-level engineering by year's end and TechCrunch reporting on entry-level job elimination, arguing jobs aren't fewer but different—requiring creativity, collaboration, and business judgment. She closes by inviting interested parties to connect as DevDay works with select design partners.
